data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'Abas' meaning 'father' and 'zia' meaning 'multitudes'. In Greek mythology, Abas was a mythical king who had many children. The name Abisia carries the meaning “Father of multitudes” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Abisia usually hope their child will grow to embody father of multitudes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the love and care of a father towards his children.
data.etymology: Abisia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Father of multitudes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abisia total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name 'Abisia' carries a royal and significant meaning in culture as it evokes the imagery of a father who has many descendants or followers. In a broad sense, it might represent a leader who nurtures, protects and guides a large community, inspiring people towards a common belief system or goal.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name 'Abisia' implies a connection to the concept of divine fatherhood, as perceived in many major world religions, including Christianity. In its essence, it serves as an inspiring reminder of God as the loving and caring father who has innumerable children, and the spiritual relationship between God, as the eternal father, and each and every human being, as his eternal creations and beloved children.
